prompt: Check a doc comment against a method signature and report which @param tags are missing and whether an @return tag is needed. Complete DocCoverageValidator and run the tests.
explanation: Validating documentation means comparing two lists: what the signature declares and what the comment mentions. Taking the last word of each comma-separated chunk is enough to name a parameter, because modifiers and types always come first -- that handles int[] values and String... parts without special cases. Keeping declaration order in the result matters, since a reviewer reads the missing tags alongside the signature.
hints: Cut the text between indexOf('(') and lastIndexOf(')'), and treat an empty result as "no parameters" before splitting on commas.
For each parameter chunk, split on whitespace with split("\\s+") and keep the last word.
The return type is the second-to-last word before the '(' -- compare it with "void" before looking for an @return tag.
